source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC / HDT Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool Test procedure: 1. BIOS settings: a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled b. UMC Common Options → DDR PMIC Configuration → PMIC Error Reporting: True c. UMC Common Options → DDR PMIC Configuration → PMIC Operation Mode: Programmable Mode d. UMC Common Options → DDR PMIC Configuration → PMIC Fault Recovery: Always e. FCH Common Options → I3C/I2C Configuration Options → Release SPD Host Control: Disabled f. FCH Common Options → I3C/I2C Configuration Options → PMFW Poll DDR5 Telemetry: Disabled g. FCH Common Options → I3C/I2C Configuration Options → I3C/I2C 0 Enable: I2C Enabled h. FCH Common Options → I3C/I2C Configuration Options → I3C/I2C 1 Enable: I2C Enabled i. FCH Common Options → I3C/I2C Configuration Options → I3C/I2C 2 Enable: I2C Enabled j. FCH Common Options → I3C/I2C Configuration Options → I3C/I2C 3 Enable: I2C Enabled 2. Unlock CPU via HDT. 3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 9.0 / Windows 2022. 4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software. 5. Enter the following commands: sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --listvalidumc 6. Fatal error injection: sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --einjpmicerrors --socketdieumc 0:0:3 --railtype 6 --voltagetype 0 --dimm 0 7.Repeat step 1 to step 6 for all DIMMs with different voltagetype as 0/1. 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed. 4. Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report.
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- VIN Mgmt to Bulk Switchover: inject the DDR PMIC VIN Mgmt to Bulk Switchover via the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool (after HDT/unlock + the BIOS RAS knobs from the procedure, e.g. Platform First Error Handling=Enabled + per-unit MCA/UMC settings). Agent stages/verifies with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -160 | grep -iE 'PMIC|power.good|critical|over.current|over.voltage|switchover|temperature|current.limit'; echo __DDR_PMIC_VIN_Mgmt_to_Bulk_Switchover; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1" but the tool injection step itself is interactive/HW-level and needs the user to drive the exact inject command.

test_case.test_name: VIN Mgmt to Bulk Switchover — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Cause the PMIC to switch from VIN_Mgmt to VIN_Bulk on every required target/comparator, verify the direction and bounded transition without unintended reset or memory corruption unless explicitly specified, and restore the intended input state.
required_package: PMIC proof railtype6 means VIN_Mgmt-to-VIN_Bulk and voltagetype0/1 trigger/comparator definitions
Decision on Fatal procedure wording versus correctable Criteria and expected reset/no-reset behavior
Per-DIMM/PMIC physical VIN_Mgmt/VIN_Bulk source and socket/die/UMC/channel/slot/dimm mapping
Wistron BMC/platform I2C controller/bus/address/OOB path and input-select/status registers
Command continuation plus complete target matrix
Transfer time, voltage-droop/interruption, downstream rail, memory-error and service-continuity limits; latch/failback and restoration
test_case.test_command: Map both physical inputs and PMIC addresses; prove railtype6/voltagetype semantics; establish VIN_Mgmt active pre-state; capture synchronized input-select, both input rails and downstream outputs; inject one tuple; measure transfer time, droop and service/memory continuity; record fresh PMIC/RAS evidence; define latch/failback; restore preferred input and platform settings before another target.
